Maintenance Report — MNT-0017-004

Asset: WELL-0017 (SW-23 Well 017, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 23 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 25 Apr 2023 17:00 · Well stopped for this job: 57 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0017-0026 on 2023-04-20 Report written: 26 Apr 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0017-0026 showed the wellhead at 33.6 °C with the air at 24.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0017-006

Asset: WELL-0017 (SW-23 Well 017, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 22 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 01 Aug 2023 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 233 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0017-0039 on 2023-07-20 Report written: 03 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0017-0039 showed the wellhead at 43.1 °C with the air at 35.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0017-009

Asset: WELL-0017 (SW-23 Well 017, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 15 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 16 Dec 2023 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 25 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0017-0059 on 2023-12-14 Report written: 18 Dec 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0017-0059 at 09:15 on 2023-12-14 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.6% of the pad area, estimated 3.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 359 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 287 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0017-009 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.7% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0017-010

Asset: WELL-0017 (SW-23 Well 017, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 30 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 Jan 2024 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 564 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0017-0061 on 2023-12-28 Report written: 23 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0017-0061 showed the wellhead at 7.1 °C with the air at 7.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,628
Bolts, shims and seals407
Bearing grease and consumables679
Labour (company crew and contractor)2,397
Total5,111

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 1 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
